why_not_copy_pilot_to_paper: One run per cell does not estimate between-run variation.
Some cross-task cells exhaust 12 calls before any validation, so quality support is incomplete.
The frozen source program and admitted definition set differ in feature content.
The source and target use different seed identifiers; the original pilot leaves adaptation to the agent.
The HTTP tool timeout is 180 seconds while the frozen Rust database pool timeout is 300 seconds, so timed-out probes may consume resources until the server deadline.
required_fixes_before_freeze: Apply the same tested identifier-only seed binding to returned programs and compiled definitions, then audit both on each target.
Use a content-matched flat-SQL control built from exactly the same frozen admitted definitions; retain the original richer source program as a separately labeled additional control.
Use one server-enforced query deadline and a slightly longer HTTP deadline for every arm; record cancellation, failed attempts and costs.

Calibrate a common 24-call/4-validation candidate budget on development data for all arms, without selecting different limits or incumbent targets by method. This value is a candidate, not a validated formal protocol.
Freeze source selection, task pairs, model/version, random order, sample IDs and independent repetition seeds before scoring final test labels.
confirmatory_outputs: Quality and valid-solution coverage for every attempted target, including failures.
Total and online costs, with source construction charged and reuse horizon stated.
Retrieval, composition, actual validation and final SQL lineage as distinct outcomes.
Paired results across independent repetitions; do not count cutoffs or requests as independent seeds.
execution_rule: Do not enlarge a known-confounded paid batch merely to obtain more figures. Complete the bounded pilot and no-LLM B/C supplements; clear the listed A gates before a separate formal run.
